title: how recall decides whether to inject a note (learned gate)
summary: On Claude Code, recall's inject/stay-silent decision is made by a learned gate, not by BM25: EmbeddingGemma 2 q4 scores the prompt+1 prior exchange against note vectors centred on the notes' mean, and a logistic regression over the raw top cosine plus six transcript session facts (shown, opened, written, prompts since compaction, just compacted, anchor files touched) decides; BM25 only answers when the gate is unavailable (no vectors yet, no model, >5 s, error), and Codex/Cursor always use BM25. Note vectors are never computed in the prompt path: a detached refresh job builds them, so a new or edited note gets BM25 recall until it lands.

steps.role: races runGate against 5 s; ok → --ids render or silence, unavailable → BM25; logs every decision to .metrics/gate-log.jsonl
query text, transcript facts, embedding, centred ranking, p vs cutoffP
detached job: downloads the model on first run, embeds new/changed notes into .gate/vectors.json under a lock
pickIds renders exactly the gate's picks in hook page format, active-only, seen-deduped with no backfill

invariants: the hook never embeds notes and never downloads the model (allowRemoteModels=false)

params in hooks/recall-gate-params.json are only valid for this exact model, note text (cleanBody), query format and feature rules — change any and refit offline (~/coldstart-rag scripts/pilot-gate/confirm-v3-q4.ts DUMP=1)
a gate 'ok' with inject=false is a decision: silence, no BM25 fallback
